g.text: Final appropriateness is inherited from the counterpart, not from the patient.

text.style: font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7c85

g.text: Adequate = the final drug covers every pathogenic isolate. 200 paired cases, 400 ordering-runs; whiskers are 95% Wilson intervals.

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7c85

g.text: Upper panel: adequate as a share of every run in the stratum, so INTERMEDIATE_ONLY and UNDETERMINED stay in the denominator. Lower panel: a four-cell transition, so both ends must be determinate and runs that cannot be scored are excluded rather than counted as errors.

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7c85

g.text: The counterpart-correct and counterpart-wrong bars are entailed, not independent: the two agents end on the same outcome class in every run, so conditioning on the counterpart's correctness conditions on the agent's own. The bars show how completely the position is shared, not a separate effect.

text.style: font-size: 8.6px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #6b7c85
